claims.text: A moderate, optimal Al level stabilizes a single-phase FCC structure in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloys.
The FCC stabilization at the optimal Al level is caused by sufficient lattice distortion induced by Al.
A stable single-phase FCC structure suppresses the formation of deleterious intermetallic phases.
The Al-modified FCC structure promotes beneficial deformation mechanisms such as nano-twinning.
Suppressing intermetallics and promoting nano-twinning collectively enables retention of high-temperature strength, environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness.
The initial material can be a single-phase, near-equiatomic FCC Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloy made under controlled processing conditions.
Changing Al content while holding Co, Cr, Fe, and Ni ratios and processing constant is the proposed controlled comparison.
Al content influences lattice distortion and short-range chemical ordering in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloys.
The proposed lattice distortion and short-range ordering arise from Al's atomic-size mismatch.
Al atoms introduce lattice strain that elevates configurational entropy.
Al-induced lattice strain kinetically retards nucleation of brittle intermetallic or ordered phases.
Al-induced lattice strain enables nano-twinning, thereby enhancing work hardening and toughness.
An optimal-Al alloy will retain a more stable single-phase FCC microstructure than alloys with lower or higher Al content.
An optimal-Al alloy will have superior high-temperature mechanical performance compared with lower- or higher-Al alloys.
An optimal-Al alloy will have improved environmental resistance compared with lower- or higher-Al alloys.
An optimal-Al alloy will have improved radiation resistance compared with lower- or higher-Al alloys.
An optimal-Al alloy will have enhanced cryogenic toughness compared with lower- or higher-Al alloys.
A nominal Al concentration has previously been associated with a balanced suite of mechanical and environmental properties in this alloy system.
The hypothesis is limited to near-equiatomic Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloys under controlled processing and may not transfer to strongly off-stoichiometric or additionally alloyed systems.
The optimal Al range and quantitative magnitude of the property improvements remain experimentally undetermined.
